sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: Choose Figure or Presentation, then start with the workspace and commands made for that document.
body: Choose Figure for one scientific canvas: manuscript panels, graphical abstracts, pathway diagrams, and illustrations. Choose Presentation for an ordered deck with a slide navigator, layouts, themes, speaker notes, and presentation controls.

Both modes use the same vector, shape, text, connector, scientific-asset, style, save, and export foundations. The document kind remains explicit when you save and reopen; adding a figure panel never silently turns a Figure into a slide deck.

Open Figure accepts an individual .fsfigure file. Open Presentation accepts an individual .fsdeck file. Open Project restores the Figure and Presentation tabs saved together in an .fsproject file. Legacy .figurestudio and .figure-studio.json files can be imported, but must be saved in a current format before they become a new save target. Open PDF/SVG starts a Figure from supported artwork; use Import when artwork should be placed into the current Figure or Presentation instead.
Use the left toolbar for authoring, the center canvas for direct manipulation, and Properties for the current selection. Advanced source details appear only when imported content needs them.

For a guided start, open Tutorials and choose a Figure, Presentation, or safe-save course. Each course saves its own progress, resumes at the first incomplete step, and offers contextual workspace callouts. Starting or resetting a tutorial never silently replaces document content.

sections.title: Switching between Figure and Presentation workspaces
sections.summary: Move between the Figure canvas and Presentation deck editor without closing documents or relaunching Figure Tool.
body: Use the always-visible Figure | Presentation switcher to change the active workspace. Figure is the single-canvas scientific illustration workspace. Presentation is the multi-slide deck editor; Present and Slideshow are commands inside that workspace, not a third document mode.

Each workspace keeps a separate tab collection. Switching to Presentation hides Figure tabs without closing them, and switching back restores the last active Figure tab. The last active Presentation tab is restored in the same way.

New Figure and Open Figure create tabs in the Figure workspace. New Presentation and Open Presentation create tabs in the Presentation workspace. Creating or opening a document can activate its appropriate workspace, but it never closes documents in the other collection.

Save, Save As, and Export are scoped to the active tab in the active workspace: .fsfigure for a Figure and .fsdeck for a Presentation. Save Project is a separate, explicit command that writes the complete open Figure and Presentation workspace to one .fsproject file.
If no tab is open in a workspace, the workspace shows a clear empty state with New and Open actions. Switching workspaces is navigation only and does not change document content or dirty state.

sections.title: Working with multiple document tabs
sections.summary: Keep several Figures and Presentations open while every tab retains its own content, history, selection, path, and dirty state.
body: The tab strip above the canvas shows documents in the active workspace. New Figure, New Presentation, Open Figure, and Open Presentation add tabs. Open Project restores a saved workspace and replaces its open Figure and Presentation tabs. Untitled documents use numbered names such as Untitled Figure 1 and Untitled Presentation 1.

A tab owns its model, filename and native path, dirty state, undo and redo history, selection, view state, save target, and export target. Changing selection or using Undo in one tab never changes another tab.
The active tab and window title show the saved filename or untitled name. A dirty marker means that tab differs from its last saved file. Saving the active tab clears only its marker.

Closing a tab with unsaved changes asks whether to discard them. Cancel keeps the tab open so you can save first. Confirming closes only that tab and discards its unsaved changes. Closing a clean tab needs no save decision.

Save each document, or use Save Project to preserve all open Figure and Presentation tabs together, before closing Figure Tool. Ordinary Save targets only the active tab. The window title also marks unsaved changes in other tabs or in a saved project's open tabs and views.
Use the Figure | Presentation switcher to reach tabs in the other workspace. Hidden tabs remain open and retain their state until you close them or exit the application.

sections.title: Creating a Figure document
sections.summary: Build one exportable scientific canvas with panels, guides, assets, labels, and artwork.
body: Choose New Figure, then select a manuscript preset, presentation-sized canvas for a graphical abstract, or a custom width and height. The artboard is the visible export boundary.
Use a multi-panel layout to add editable panel frames and labels. Align and distribute the frames, replace placeholders with results or assets, and keep labels in their own layer for easier editing.

A Figure has one primary canvas. It does not show a slide navigator or deck-only controls. Save Figure preserves the artboard, objects, layers, styles, embedded assets, and supported source attachments.

Run Figure check before final export to find overset text, missing linked artwork, low-resolution images, unsupported effects, or content outside the artboard. Figure check advises; it does not silently rewrite artwork.

sections.title: Artboards, panels, and figure layouts
sections.summary: Size a Figure canvas and organize multi-panel artwork without introducing slide behavior.
body: The Figure artboard defines the exported page. Use a preset or enter a custom size; changing the artboard does not scale artwork unless you choose an explicit scale-with-artboard action.
Multi-panel layouts create ordinary editable frames and panel labels. They can be resized, aligned, restyled, grouped, or removed like other objects.
Use guides, margins, Align, and Distribute to maintain consistent gutters. Content outside the artboard remains editable but is excluded from normal Figure export.

sections.title: Creating a Presentation document
sections.summary: Author an ordered scientific slide deck with consistent size, layouts, themes, notes, and playback.
body: Choose New Presentation, then select the slide size and an optional theme. Every slide in a Presentation uses the same deck geometry; creating a slide does not reset the deck to a Figure preset.

Use the navigator to create, duplicate, reorder, and delete slides. Apply a layout to the current slide, then edit its text, images, scientific assets, shapes, vectors, and connectors with the shared authoring tools.
Themes provide coordinated colors, type choices, and layout defaults. Applying a theme does not flatten custom artwork. Review slides after a theme or layout change when exact text wrapping matters.

Speaker notes belong to their slide and reopen with the Presentation. Present from beginning or Present from current slide fits the complete slide inside the available stage and keeps navigation and Exit controls reachable.

Save Presentation preserves slide order, slide size, themes, layouts, notes, and editable artwork. Export PDF for dependable sharing, or use bounded PPTX interchange when collaborators need editable common content.

sections.title: Managing slides, layouts, themes, and notes
sections.summary: Keep a scientific deck coherent while each slide remains independently editable.
body: New Slide uses the selected layout and the Presentation's established slide size. Duplicate Slide copies the current slide and notes. Drag in the navigator or use Move Up and Move Down to reorder; Delete Slide asks for confirmation when it would discard work.
Layouts are starting structures, not locked templates. Replace placeholders with live text, images, vectors, or scientific assets and adjust them with the normal selection and alignment tools.

Use a theme for consistent fonts and colors, then keep deliberate slide-specific overrides where needed. Theme changes do not promise identical rendering in PowerPoint or Google Slides; review exported files in the destination application.
Add speaker notes below the slide. Notes are included in the Figure Tool document and the supported PPTX notes subset when available, but are excluded from normal slide PDF, SVG, and PNG output.

sections.title: Presenting and reviewing slide playback
sections.summary: Review a deck in fitted playback while keeping navigation, speaker notes, and Exit controls reachable.
body: Present from beginning starts with slide 1. Present from current slide starts with the selected navigator item. Both commands belong to the active Presentation tab and use that deck's current slide order.
Playback fits the complete slide inside the available stage without cropping its edges. Resizing the window recalculates the fit; it does not change slide geometry, artwork size, or the saved deck.
Use the visible navigation controls or supported keyboard commands to move between slides. The slide counter, Notes control, and Exit remain reachable at supported desktop sizes.
Speaker notes display for the current slide when Notes is open. Notes are presenter guidance, not visible slide artwork, and normal slide images or PDFs do not include them.
Exit returns to the same Presentation tab and slide. Playback does not save, export, flatten, or otherwise change the document.
Review every slide for overflow, small type, source legibility, transitions in scientific reasoning, and unintended off-slide content before exporting or presenting to an audience.

sections.title: Opening and importing SVG, PDF, and images
sections.summary: Open supported artwork as a Figure, or place it into the current Figure or Presentation.
body: Use Open PDF/SVG when imported artwork should become a new Figure. Figure Tool sizes the artboard to the opened page or artwork and keeps the supported original source available under Source & notes.

Use Import when SVG, image, or PDF artwork should be placed into the current Figure or slide. Review placement and size, then place the artwork; it remains selected so you can align or resize it immediately.

For an editable PDF page, choose Direct Selection or press A, then click artwork inside the page. You can also double-click the page to enter its contents. PDF text opens as vector outlines by default so the page keeps its original appearance.

Select the PDF page and use PDF text > Convert to editable text when wording must change. Figure Tool reconstructs detected text runs and keeps the outline representation available through Keep outlines. Figure check reports substituted fonts, symbols, spacing, and rotated labels that need review before export.

The original PDF remains attached at the document level even after individual page objects are released or deleted. Dense or complex sources may stay protected, with editable overlays for supported changes. Technical source details are available under Advanced.
Raster imports are embedded as images. Raster vectorization can create editable regions, but it is segmentation of pixels, not biological interpretation.

sections.title: PowerPoint and Google Slides compatibility
sections.summary: Use PPTX for bounded editable deck interchange, with explicit warnings when content is flattened or skipped.
body: PPTX v1 imports and exports slide order and one uniform slide size; plain text boxes; rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, and triangles; straight lines and connectors; embedded PNG, JPEG, and SVG images; basic solid fills and strokes; basic arrowheads; and plain speaker notes.

Text interchange includes the text object's base font family, size, bold, italic, alignment, and solid color. Superscript, subscript, baseline shift, and other mixed character-range formatting remain editable in the Figure Tool document and visual exports, but PPTX v1 reduces those ranges to the base supported text style and reports a warning. Basic theme colors are resolved when a PPTX is imported. Content inherited from a PowerPoint master or layout is not imported; objects drawn directly on slides remain editable within the supported subset.

On export, supported Fabric vector or grouped artwork that is not directly representable in the bounded subset can be placed as an embedded SVG with a warning. Content that cannot be represented or safely flattened is skipped with a warning instead of being silently misreported as editable.

SmartArt, charts, tables, audio, video, 3D objects, animations, transitions, macros, OLE objects, arbitrary freeform paths, and advanced theme or master effects are outside PPTX v1. Import reports these items plainly and leaves the original file unchanged.

Google Slides compatibility is file-based: import or export PPTX for common editable content, or use PDF, SVG, and PNG for visual sharing. Figure Tool 1.0.0-beta.6 has no direct Google Drive or Google Slides cloud connection.
Always review an exported PPTX in the destination application. Figure Tool does not claim universal PowerPoint or Google Slides round-trip fidelity.

sections.title: Selecting and arranging objects
sections.summary: Use the canvas, context menus, and layer tree to select, group, hide, lock, reorder, and move objects through a document hierarchy.
body: Named layers are saved with the Figure or with each slide. Click a layer header to make it current; new shapes, text, imports, and pasted artwork are inserted there. Use Move here or a layer context menu to move the current top-level selection without changing its geometry.

Drag an editable object or ordinary group in Layers to place it before, inside, or after a compatible destination. The highlighted destination names the result before you drop. Moving artwork between groups or named layers keeps its position on the canvas and is one undoable action. Locked, protected, source-backed, self, descendant, and structurally incompatible destinations are rejected with a plain explanation.

Click objects on the canvas or select rows in Layers. Shift-click rows for multi-selection. Use Reveal in Layers on selected canvas artwork to open the panel and expose its exact row. Use Select on canvas from a row to select that object; Fit selection brings off-screen artwork into view without changing document geometry. Right-click selected artwork or object rows for duplicate, delete, group, ungroup, layer-bounded arrange, lock, hide, and properties actions. Alt+Page Up or Alt+Page Down changes the current layer; add Shift to move the selection to the adjacent layer.

Layer visibility and lock state apply to all of that layer's artwork while preserving each object's own hidden or locked state. Layer order defines the major stacking bands, and object arrange commands stay inside their layer. Expand groups to browse and rename nested objects; selecting a nested row enters the required Isolation Mode path without flattening the group.
Object rows identify groups, editable vectors, protected source artwork, clips, masks, filters, blend modes, gradients, and patterns when Figure Tool can detect them.

Large PDF or SVG imports are windowed in the layer list so thousands of objects do not render as thousands of rows at once. Use Advanced source parts when you need to inspect individual imported elements.

sections.title: Selection, transforms, align, and distribute
sections.summary: Choose whole objects or individual vector parts, then position them precisely or as a coordinated selection.
body: Use Selection or V to move, resize, rotate, duplicate, group, and arrange whole objects. Shift-click adds or removes objects from the selection. Drag a marquee across empty canvas to select several objects.

Use Direct Selection or A to edit supported anchors, handles, line endpoints, connector bends, and children inside groups or imported vectors. Double-click a group to enter Isolation Mode; use Back or Escape to return to the containing artwork.

Enter exact X, Y, width, height, rotation, line length, or angle values in Properties. Multi-selection transforms preserve the objects' relative placement. Lock proportions when width and height should change together.

Align uses the selection, the artboard or slide, or a chosen key object as its reference. A key object stays fixed while the other selected objects move. Enter an exact horizontal or vertical gap when repeated panels or diagram nodes need a specific gutter.

In Figure documents, Duplicate and Repeat creates a copy using the last safe move, rotation, or proportional scale; Transform Again reuses that transform on the current selection. Repeat is kept with its own document tab and is unavailable for protected, linked, connected, or otherwise unsafe artwork.

View provides separate Snap to Grid, Snap to Guides, and Snap to Objects choices. Snap to Objects includes object edges and centers, equal-spacing positions, and artboard edges and centers. Smart Guides control the temporary alignment and spacing cues; hiding those cues does not turn off any snap channel.
Hold Ctrl while moving, scaling, or drawing to bypass all snapping for that gesture. On macOS, hold Command. Release the key to use the saved snap choices again.
Group related labels and artwork when they should move together. Layers and groups retain their names, order, visibility, and lock state when the document is saved and reopened.

sections.title: Shapes, pen tools, paths, and nodes
sections.summary: Draw basic shapes and freeform paths, then refine supported anchors, handles, and combined geometry.
body: Use the Shape tools for rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, polygons, stars, lines, and arrows. Drag on the canvas for a visual size or use Properties for exact geometry. Hold Shift where offered to constrain proportions or direction.

Use Pen to click straight anchors and drag curved handles. Close a path by returning to its first anchor, or finish an open path with Enter. Use Direct Selection to move anchors and handles, convert supported point types, add or remove nodes, and edit one path without moving the whole object.

Press A for Direct Selection, then click inside supported imported PDF or SVG artwork to select a text outline, path, shape, or image. On dense protected artwork, Figure Tool creates an editable overlay while keeping the original available through Restore source. Double-clicking editable imported artwork also enters its contents.

Select two or more closed editable shapes and choose Shape Builder to combine highlighted regions; hold Alt while clicking or dragging to remove regions. Divide creates the visible regions as separate editable artwork. Protected, open, grouped, or locked artwork must be released or made editable first.

Lines and arrows expose endpoints with exact start, end, length, and angle values in Properties. When one endpoint is selected with Direct Selection, the opposite endpoint becomes the pivot for length and angle changes.
Advanced PDF details can expose native path operations when Figure Tool has safely identified a contiguous PDF path sequence. These controls are not part of the normal editing workflow.
Deleting an isolated source edit keeps the replaced source element hidden until you choose Restore source. Duplicated overlays become independent artwork.
Ordinary SVG files and older documents can use geometric fallback selection. Figure Tool does not provide unrestricted freeform editing of every possible PDF content stream.

sections.title: Authoring scientific connectors
sections.summary: Attach scientific relationships to object ports, refine their route directly, and keep connector semantics editable through figure production.
body: Choose Smart Connector, then select a start and end port. Eligible objects expose three ports on each side so dense pathway figures can separate nearby relationships without enlarging the visible markers. Straight, elbow, and curved routes use the connector's stroke, dash, start marker, end marker, and optional label settings.

Selection and Direct Selection have separate jobs. Use Selection to choose the connector as one object. Press A for Direct Selection to expose its two endpoint handles and, for elbow routes, its bend handles. The visible controls stay small while their pointer targets remain at least 24 pixels at supported desktop sizes.

Drag an endpoint onto another port to reattach it, or drag into open canvas to detach only that endpoint. Hold Shift to constrain the drag to one axis. Hold Alt, Ctrl, or Command to bypass object ports and snapping for a free endpoint. A selected endpoint can be nudged with the arrow keys, with Shift for ten-unit steps; Delete detaches it without deleting the connector. Reverse swaps the biological direction while preserving the start and end marker style slots.

Drag or nudge an elbow bend to enter manual routing. Shift constrains bend movement to one axis, while Alt, Ctrl, or Command bypasses snapping. Orthogonal keeps manual legs axis-aligned. Auto returns the connector to bounded obstacle- and label-aware routing. Automatic routing reports constrained cases honestly; it does not claim global pathway layout, arbitrary maze solving, or semantic crossing resolution.

Connector labels are normal selectable text objects. Move or nudge a label to create a durable offset from its routed segment, edit its text directly, or choose Label home to restore automatic placement. Moving attached nodes updates the route; a fully detached connector can be moved as one object with Selection.

Endpoint identities, ports, route mode, bends, styles, labels, and label offsets participate in undo and redo. They persist through grouping, duplication with remapped endpoint identities, Save Figure or Save Presentation and reopen, and SVG, PNG, and PDF export.

sections.title: Editing typography and text paths
sections.summary: Format selected characters, coordinate publication text roles, insert scientific symbols, work with fixed area text and text paths, and create reversible outlines.
body: Select live text to use Character controls for font, size, leading, tracking, bold, italic, underline, and strikethrough. Paragraph controls provide alignment, justification, and left-to-right or right-to-left direction.

While editing text, select the characters that should be raised or lowered, then choose Superscript or Subscript in Character. These are real character-range styles: the surrounding text stays unchanged, the two choices are mutually exclusive, and choosing an active style again removes it. With only a caret, the choice applies to characters you type next.

Baseline shift moves only the selected characters without changing their font size, family, color, or other styling. Values are measured in points: a positive value raises text and a negative value lowers it. Reset returns the selected characters to their normal baseline while leaving superscript or subscript sizing intact.

Choose Symbols to search common Greek letters, mathematical and statistical notation, arrows, and scientific units by symbol or name. Insertion replaces the current character selection or occurs at the caret, then returns to text editing. Recently used symbols appear first. Use Unicode only for the actual symbol; use Superscript and Subscript for raised or lowered letters and numbers.

Tracking changes spacing across the selected text object. For a manual kerning pair, enter text editing, place the cursor between two characters, then adjust Kerning in Properties. Manual pair spacing remains attached to that text object across project reload.

Drag with the Text tool to create a fixed area text frame. Text reflows when the frame width changes, while a small plus badge and the Properties status identify overset text. Fit frame to content grows the frame height without changing its width.

To place text on a path, select one ordinary editable text object and one ordinary editable path, then choose Type > Type on a Path or use the object context menu. Character-range formatting stays with the text when it is placed on or detached from the path. Adjust the start offset and path alignment in Properties. Flip Path Text Side moves readable text to the opposite side; Detach from Path restores separate editable text and path objects.

Save Figure and Save Presentation preserve character-range formatting through reopen, copy, duplicate, undo, and redo. SVG, PDF, PNG, JPEG, and TIFF preserve the visible raised and lowered characters. PPTX v1 keeps the text editable but reduces character-range formatting to the text object's base supported style; review scientific notation after PPTX interchange.

Create Outlines converts supported live text to editable vector glyph paths. Figure Tool retains the source text, font metadata, and scene position in the project so Restore Editable Text can reverse the command. Current outline shaping uses direct font glyph mapping; complex scripts, per-range styles, and advanced OpenType shaping require further support.

PDF text identifies its detected source font and whether Figure Tool retained that exact embeddable font, fitted a replacement, or must use the vector-outline fallback. Source-font outlines use the retained font program when available. Typography changes and outlines are canvas edits with review status; they do not claim native PDF text-stream mutation or full Illustrator/PDF equivalence.

For a Figure, choose Type > Publication typography to review one publisher-neutral profile for panel labels, titles, annotations, and legend/body text. Panel Label objects are recognized automatically; select other editable text before opening the dialog and assign its role explicitly. The preview lists exact final-size points, weight, line height, color, font resolution, page locations, possible reflow or overset, and report-only protected content before it changes anything.

Reviewed panel-label renumbering follows page order and then left-to-right, top-to-bottom position. Apply updates linked named text styles as one undo step while preserving live text, scientific Unicode, character-range superscript or subscript, object identity, position, groups, layers, and unrelated artwork. Save Figure preserves the profile, roles, style bindings, and label sequence. SVG and PDF record review metadata, but Figure Tool does not claim font installation or embedding, complex-script shaping, publisher certification, or cross-application typographic equivalence.

sections.title: Building an appearance stack
sections.summary: Layer fills, strokes, gradients, patterns, blend modes, and bounded effects while keeping one editable vector path.
body: Select an ordinary editable shape or path, then use Appearance in Properties or the Object menu. The top row is the frontmost item. Move rows forward or backward to control how paints and effects overlap.

Fill and stroke rows can use a solid color, linear gradient, radial gradient, or diagonal, crosshatch, and dot pattern. Gradient rows expose every color stop with location, opacity, and a midpoint for the segment that follows it. Add, remove, or reorder stops in Properties.

Press G or choose Edit on canvas to use the Gradient tool. Drag linear start/end geometry or radial center/radius geometry, drag interior color stops to reorder them along the axis, and drag the small midpoint diamonds to bias color interpolation. Double-click the gradient axis to add a stop; select an interior stop and press Delete to remove it.

Every item has its own visibility, opacity, and blend mode. Stroke rows also have an independent width. Offset Copy creates a live vector-representable duplicate; Soft Shadow adds a bounded blur and remains live.

Expand Appearance replaces eligible solid, gradient, and offset-copy stacks with grouped ordinary vector objects. Pattern tiles and soft shadows disable expansion because silently flattening them would not produce ordinary editable path geometry. Reduce to Base Appearance keeps the frontmost fill and stroke and removes the extra stack entries.

Figure Tool stores up to eight appearance items on one eligible vector and up to eight authored stops in one gradient. Eyedropper and Graphic Styles retain the full appearance. Save and reopen preserve the ordered items; SVG and PDF export retain supported gradients, blends, and soft blur.

This stack applies to ordinary editable vector shapes and paths. Lines, arrows, text, groups, protected source artwork, and native PDF objects keep their dedicated appearance workflows. Appearance changes do not rewrite arbitrary native PDF content.

sections.title: Reusing Graphic Styles
sections.summary: Save an editable vector appearance once, then apply or merge it across eligible figure objects.
body: Select one ordinary editable shape or path, open Appearance in Properties, name the style, and choose Save style. The style records the ordered fills, strokes, gradients, patterns, blend modes, and supported effects rather than a flattened preview.

Choose a thumbnail to replace the current appearance of every eligible selected vector. Choose the plus button or Merge to put the style paints in front of each object's current appearance. A merged stack keeps at most eight items, and Figure Tool reports any omitted back paints.

Manage document styles in My Assets. Built-in styles remain available, while saved styles can be renamed or deleted. Custom styles and the last-used style are preserved by Save Figure and Save Presentation and participate in undo history.

Graphic Styles apply only to ordinary editable vector shapes and paths. Locked, text, line, group, protected imported, and native PDF objects are skipped and counted. Applying a Graphic Style never rewrites a native PDF content stream and does not claim Illustrator/PDF native equivalence.

sections.title: Using swatches and Recolor Selection
sections.summary: Build document color groups, link artwork to global colors, and preview coordinated color changes before committing them.
body: Open Swatches from the Object menu or the Inspector tab. A swatch can be applied to fills, strokes, live text, either arrowhead, or the selected stop in an ordinary editable gradient.

Global colors stay linked to the artwork that uses them. Editing a Global swatch updates linked objects, gradient stops, patterns, and saved Graphic Styles. Process colors apply the current value without keeping a live link.
Use Select > Same Fill Color, Same Stroke Color, or Same Global Swatch to find matching artwork. Select an editable SVG group and choose Collect to add its unique colors to a Collected color group.

Recolor Selection creates a live preview for ordinary editable artwork. Map source colors to custom values or document swatches, preserve neutrals when appropriate, then Apply colors or Cancel to restore the exact starting appearance.

Saved Figure and Presentation documents retain the swatch library. SVG export retains supported document colors, while PDF export uses the resolved vector colors. Protected PDF artwork remains unchanged unless it has first become ordinary editable vectors.

sections.title: Creating editable vector patterns
sections.summary: Create a named repeating tile from ordinary vectors, tune its bounds and spacing, and reuse it as a live Appearance fill.
body: Select one to eight ordinary editable vector shapes or paths, open Swatches, and choose Create in the Patterns section. Figure Tool keeps the selected source artwork on the canvas and adds a named vector tile to the document library.

Select an ordinary editable target and choose the pattern thumbnail to apply it. A named pattern remains linked across Appearance fills and saved Graphic Styles. Rename or delete it in Swatches; deleting a library entry leaves existing artwork with an unlinked copy of its current tile.

Choose Edit beside a named pattern in Appearance, or use Object > Edit Pattern Tile. Pattern Edit shows small handles for the tile origin, tile bounds, horizontal spacing, and vertical spacing. The visible markers stay small while their pointer targets remain larger. Use Commit or Enter to keep the edit, and Cancel or Escape to restore the starting tile across linked uses.

Saved Figure and Presentation documents preserve the named vector library. SVG export writes a reusable vector pattern resource, and PDF export uses that vector output. Opening an exported SVG or PDF does not reconstruct the named Figure Tool pattern library; imported artwork follows the normal editable-vector or protected-source path.

Pattern authoring is limited to ordinary editable vectors and bounded tile markup. It does not write native PDF Pattern resources, gradient meshes, ICC or spot-color resources, or claim full Illustrator/PDF equivalence.

sections.title: Brushes and variable-width strokes
sections.summary: Apply reusable width, calligraphic, vector-art, or scientific motif brushes to an open or closed path.
body: Select an editable single-subpath vector path, line, or arrow and open Appearance in Properties. The Brushes section provides compact previews for built-in and document brushes. Applying a brush sets the base stroke width, cap, join, and width profile.

Choose Width Tool or press Shift+W. Each width point has a round left-side handle and a diamond right-side handle. Turn Link sides off to edit either side independently; leave it on for symmetric edits. Small visible handles retain larger pointer targets. Click the path to add a point, use the arrow keys to nudge the selected side, and press Delete to remove an interior point. Closed paths use one cyclic seam point. Enter commits; Escape restores the starting profile.

Choose Brush Options from Appearance, the Object menu, a path context menu, or the Width Tool strip. Width Profile keeps the current per-side shape. Calligraphic provides a fixed nib angle and roundness. Art Brush provides reusable ribbon presets or selected vector artwork. New Art Brush from Selection captures up to eight ordinary vector objects or nested groups, with up to 24 visible vector children, while leaving the source artwork and grouping unchanged on the artboard.

Selected-art options control direction, mirroring along or across the path, fit or stretch-between-guides behavior, corner overlap adjustment, and tint, tints-and-shades, or preserved source colors. The brush source is stored as bounded vector paths, and the same warped vector pieces are used for canvas display and export.

Scientific Motif artwork repeats an original first-party vector motif along the same editable path model. Built-in motifs cover phospholipid mono- and bilayers, double- and single-stranded nucleic acid, a vessel or tubule wall, actin, and microtubules. Brush Options keeps spacing, scale, path direction, side, orientation, and motif-specific color roles explicit. The selected motif's intended scientific limits remain visible in the editor and stored with the live object.

Choose Expand Art Brush to Paths from Properties, Object, or the path context menu when you need ordinary editable geometry. Expansion replaces the live brush path with a grouped set of normal vector paths at the same layer position. Enter Isolation Mode or ungroup the result to edit individual anchors. The expanded paths no longer depend on the brush definition.

Graphic Styles retain supported width profiles. Saved documents and undo history retain brushes, brush options, expanded groups, motif source and rights records, and per-object left and right widths. SVG export compiles live strokes and motifs into vector geometry; expanded brushes export as ordinary paths, and PDF export uses the same geometry.

Scientific Motif editing recommends source paths no longer than 4,800 pt, with no more than 240 motif placements or 960 generated vector paths. Live rendering is bounded at 512 motifs and 2,400 paths. When a dense or long brush exceeds a recommendation or reaches a cap, Figure Tool reports the requested and rendered counts and suggests increasing spacing or shortening the path instead of silently rasterizing the brush.

This release supports solid strokes on ordinary editable single-subpath vectors. Grouped selected-art sources may contain ordinary paths and basic shapes; convert text to outlines and expand gradients, patterns, live effects, masks, blends, dashed or variable strokes first. Raster images and protected PDF objects are rejected instead of being silently rasterized. Arrowheads must be removed or separately expanded before expanding an Art Brush. Scatter, bristle, pressure or stylus variation, compound-subpath offset cleanup, and robust cleanup of self-intersecting warped geometry remain outside this brush engine.

Scientific motifs are schematic composition aids, not molecular, compositional, directional, compartment, interaction, or scale evidence. Brush editing does not mutate an attached PDF content stream or claim native Illustrator/PDF brush equivalence. Protected and native PDF objects must first become ordinary editable vectors before Figure Tool brush controls apply.

sections.title: Using clips and masks
sections.summary: Author editable clipping masks and compound paths while preserving unsupported imported compositing.
body: For ordinary editable vectors, place the intended clipping path above the content, select them together, then choose Object > Make Clipping Mask or press Ctrl+7. Layers shows the clipping path separately from the clipped contents. Use Edit Clipping Path for Direct Selection, Edit Clipped Contents for isolation mode, and Release Clipping Mask to return every item to the canvas.

Select two or more editable paths and choose Object > Make Compound Path or press Ctrl+8. The resulting path uses an even-odd fill rule, exposes all subpath anchors to Direct Selection, and can be separated again with Release Compound Path.

Figure Tool detects clip paths and masks in supported SVG and PDF artwork when those relationships can be represented safely. Direct Selection identifies the clipping path, masked content, and protected imported structures.
Safe actions include selecting represented structures, hiding or locking protected bounds, and releasing imported structures when a normal editable form is available.
The original PDF or SVG appearance remains authoritative for unsupported compositing. Figure Tool does not claim arbitrary editing of every native mask or effect graph.

sections.title: Using assets, scenes and templates
sections.summary: Find scientific assets, insert an editable scene, or create a new figure from a layout template.
body: Library opens with Assets first, followed by Scenes and Templates. Search stays at the top and applies to the selected view. Assets provides individual scientific symbols; Scenes provides complete editable diagrams with previews and short scientific summaries.
Choose Templates to create a new Figure from a layout. Earlier figures stay open in their own tabs.

Use as new figure opens the complete scene on a new Figure canvas. Insert in this figure adds it to the current Figure; Insert on this slide adds editable artwork without changing the Presentation or creating another slide.

Scene labels are placeholders you can edit directly. Scientific assets, relationships, and labels remain separate on named layers, so you can move a module, reconnect a relationship, or remove an unneeded branch without rebuilding the scene.
Use Assets to search names, tags, and common scientific synonyms. Favorites and Recent keep frequently used concepts close at hand in both Figure and Presentation documents.

Select a scientific asset to recolor its named parts. When a concept offers another drawing, switch its style or use Replace; its position, size, scene layer, and attached relationships are preserved.
Scientific assets remain editable vector groups after insertion. Release editable paths only when you need detailed geometry changes, because the released paths no longer behave as one library asset.

sections.title: Results panels, images, and small tables
sections.summary: Place result panels, frame images in Figures or Presentations without changing their source pixels, and add small publication tables.
body: Import a result SVG, image, or PDF as artwork, then use Link Selected Panel when you want its source relationship recorded under Source & notes. Updating a linked panel is explicit. If a source is unavailable, the panel reports that state instead of silently replacing local work.

Image Frame is a shared Figure and Presentation capability. Select an eligible embedded image on a Figure canvas or Presentation slide to use Fit, Fill, the nine-position focal control, or Reset. The frame keeps its visible bounds while the image is fitted or cropped, and stores those choices with that document so the source pixels remain available after save and reopen.

Figure-only precision arrangement controls, including exact gaps and repeated transforms, do not appear in Presentation. Image Frame appears contextually in either workspace only for an eligible selected image. Locked artwork must be unlocked, and protected or source-backed artwork must be released before reframing.
File > Import CSV/TSV Table creates a small, bounded publication table card. It is intended for concise result tables, not spreadsheet calculation or bulk data editing.

sections.title: Reusing scientific components
sections.summary: Save an authored scientific module once, insert linked instances, and vary bounded biological labels or appearance without losing master geometry updates.
body: Group an ordinary authored scientific module, open My Assets, name it under Scientific components, and choose Save group. The library keeps a thumbnail, stable internal part identities, and a revisioned editable master. Insert places the next instance beside existing copies so receptor, organelle, pathway, or assay modules can be compared without an overlapping stack.

Select an instance and open Instance overrides in the inspector. Text, simple fill and stroke colors, visibility, and opacity can vary by named part. Those bounded overrides remain local when Update master sends geometry changes to every linked instance. Reset restores one part or the entire instance; Detach converts the instance into an intentional local copy.

Rename or delete masters in My Assets. Deleting a master detaches existing instances rather than removing artwork. Duplicate, group, undo, redo, save/reopen, and SVG, PNG, and PDF rendering preserve component artwork and supported overrides.

Results-linked panels, protected imported artwork, native PDF content, locked descendants, and nested components cannot become a component master. Release or redraw protected artwork explicitly first. Component overrides are intentionally bounded and do not claim full Illustrator symbol-property equivalence.

sections.title: Saving the active document with Save and Save As
sections.summary: Save the active Figure or Presentation in its own current format, or explicitly save all open tabs together as a Figure Tool Project.
body: Save and Save As apply only to the active tab: an individual Figure uses .fsfigure and an individual Presentation uses .fsdeck. They never silently modify another tab or the other workspace.

In the desktop app, Save on an untitled document opens the native Windows file dialog. Choose a filename and location. After a successful write, the tab and window title show that filename and the document's dirty marker clears.

In the desktop app, later Save writes the active document to its established path without asking for another name. Save As opens the native dialog and, after success, makes the chosen filename and path the active tab's new save target.

The confirmation uses ordinary language and identifies exactly what was saved and where—for example, Saved “Mechanism figure.fsfigure” in “C:\Research\Figures”. If writing fails, the document stays dirty and Figure Tool does not claim that it was saved.
In a browser, Figure Tool downloads a named .fsfigure or .fsdeck file. The browser controls its destination. The confirmation identifies the filename; later Save downloads another copy.

Save Project and Save Project As are separate commands for preserving all open Figure and Presentation tabs in one .fsproject file. Saving an individual tab does not silently update a project file, and saving a project does not change the individual tab's Save target.

Legacy .figurestudio and .figure-studio.json files are import-only. After reviewing an imported legacy document, use Save As to create a current .fsfigure or .fsdeck file. Export As creates delivery files such as SVG, PDF, PNG, TIFF, JPEG, or PPTX and does not establish a document Save target.

sections.title: Saving, reopening, and recovering work
sections.summary: Reopen individual Figure and Presentation files or restore an explicitly saved multi-document project, with clear legacy-import and unsaved-work safeguards.
body: Use Save for the active Figure or Presentation. In the desktop app, an untitled tab opens Save As; a named tab writes to its existing path. Save As asks for a name and location and assigns that target to the active tab. In a browser, Save downloads a named file and the browser controls its destination.

Current files make their scope explicit: .fsfigure contains one Figure, .fsdeck contains one Presentation, and .fsproject contains the open Figure and Presentation workspace. Legacy .figurestudio and .figure-studio.json files open only for import; review the mode and content, then use Save As to create a current-format copy.

New Figure, New Presentation, Open Figure, and Open Presentation add tabs. Open Project replaces the open Figure and Presentation workspace. Save each document or use Save Project before replacing the workspace or closing Figure Tool. Cancel a tab's close confirmation to keep editing or save first. Import places supported artwork into the current document.

Embedded images and released scientific assets reopen without their original repository paths. Linked artwork that cannot be found appears as a labeled missing item with its last saved placement and Source & notes information.

If Figure Tool offers a recovery copy after an interruption, open it as a separate tab, review the document kind and content, then use Save As. Recovery is a safety copy, not a promise that every unsaved change survives, and not a substitute for deliberate saved versions and ordinary backups.

sections.title: Exporting a Figure with format and resolution controls
sections.summary: Export the active Figure as vector or raster output with controls that match the selected format and intended delivery size.
body: Choose Export As while the intended Figure tab is active. The dialog names that document and offers Figure formats only. Export does not act on other Figure tabs or on any Presentation.

SVG and PDF are vector outputs and do not expose DPI controls. Use SVG when supported editable paths are useful downstream, or PDF for a portable publication page. Review fonts, clipping, masks, gradients, and imported content in the destination viewer.

PNG, JPEG, and TIFF are raster outputs. Choose a useful 96, 150, 300, or 600 DPI preset, an equivalent scale, or explicit pixel dimensions. The dialog shows the resulting dimensions so physical size and resolution are not confused with canvas zoom.

Choose transparent or solid background only when the selected format supports it. JPEG is opaque. PNG and TIFF can preserve transparency where the current renderer and destination format support it; always inspect edge antialiasing over the intended final background.

For documents with applicable artboard scope, choose Current artboard or All artboards. A multi-artboard raster export uses a coherent multi-file destination or package and names outputs predictably instead of silently overwriting them.

Run Figure check before final export. After completion, the status message identifies the Figure filename or untitled name, selected format, scope when relevant, and real destination path. Browser fallback identifies only the downloaded filename.

sections.title: Exporting a Presentation and its slides
sections.summary: Export the active deck as PPTX or PDF, or render the current slide or all slides as consistently named raster files.
body: Choose Export As while the intended Presentation tab is active. The dialog names that deck and offers Presentation formats only. Figure documents and other Presentation tabs remain untouched.
Export PDF creates one page per slide in navigator order. PDF is the dependable visual share; review every page for clipping, font substitution, and unintended off-slide artwork.

Export PPTX uses the documented v1 interchange subset. Read the supported, approximated, and unsupported summary before export, review every warning, and inspect the exported file in PowerPoint or another PPTX consumer. Universal round-trip fidelity is not claimed.

For PNG, JPEG, or TIFF, choose Current slide or All slides and set a useful resolution or explicit dimensions. Current slide produces one file. All slides uses a selected folder or package choice and predictable slide-numbered filenames without overwriting unrelated files.

Raster background and transparency follow format support: JPEG is opaque, while PNG or TIFF can offer transparency where supported. The same dimensions and background choices apply consistently to every slide in an All slides export.

After completion, the status message identifies the Presentation, selected format, current or all slide scope, and destination. Browser fallback reports explicit downloaded filenames but does not claim to know the browser's destination folder.

sections.title: Exporting PNG, SVG, PDF, and PPTX
sections.summary: Choose an output for publication, sharing, or bounded editable deck interchange.
body: For a Figure, Export As offers SVG and PDF vector output plus PNG, JPEG, and TIFF raster output. Raster formats offer useful resolution presets or explicit dimensions and format-appropriate background controls; vector formats do not show meaningless DPI controls.
For a Presentation, export PDF or bounded PPTX, or render the current slide or all slides as PNG, JPEG, or TIFF with consistent resolution settings and coherent multi-file naming.

Export PPTX when collaborators need common editable slide content. The bounded PPTX v1 subset covers ordinary text, basic shapes, lines and connectors, embedded PNG/JPEG/SVG images, one uniform slide size, slide order, and plain speaker notes. Read PowerPoint and Google Slides compatibility before relying on interchange.

Run Figure check before export. Address missing artwork, overset text, low-resolution images, unsupported effects, or off-canvas content, then open the exported file in its destination application for a final visual review.

Saving a Figure Tool document and exporting an output are different actions. Save and Export target only the active tab. Keep the editable Figure or Presentation document even when PDF, SVG, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, or PPTX is the file you deliver.

sections.title: Finding help and resuming guided tutorials
sections.summary: Use the hierarchical Help Center for reference and the separate guided curriculum for step-by-step practice across both workspaces.
body: Open Help for task-first reference. Expand the table of contents by area, search all local articles, or open a contextual Learn action from a tool or dialog. Help search is local and read-only; it does not change the active document.
Back and Forward move through the articles and tutorials visited during the current learning session. Related topics connect adjacent tasks without forcing you back to the top of the contents.

Every article has a stable #help/topic deep link. A deep link opens the owned Figure Tool article even when the app is installed offline. Tutorial links use #tutorial/course/step so a supported learning route can return to a particular course step.

Tutorials are a separate guided curriculum covering a first Figure, four-panel Figure, asset diagram, vector editing, imported SVG/PDF, publication export, first Presentation, layouts/themes, PPTX interchange, and save/recovery.

Each course stores its own completed steps and resumes at the first incomplete step. Continue marks the current step complete. Back changes the viewed step. Restart clears only that course's progress and never deletes or replaces document content.

Show in workspace is an explicit learner action. New tutorial documents open as additional tabs. If a future tutorial step would replace dirty content, Figure Tool defaults to keeping the current document and requires a separate explicit discard choice.

sections.title: Shortcuts and accessibility
sections.summary: Use keyboard authoring and visible focus while preserving a readable scientific workspace.
body: Common shortcuts include V for Selection, A for Direct Selection, T for Text, P for Pen, G for Gradient, Ctrl+Z for Undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z for Redo, Ctrl+D for Duplicate, Ctrl+G for Group, Ctrl+Shift+G for Ungroup, and Delete for an unlocked selection.

Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move through menus, panels, fields, and dialogs. Enter activates the focused control; Escape closes a menu or dialog, cancels an in-progress direct edit, or leaves Isolation Mode when offered.
Arrow keys nudge selected artwork; Shift+Arrow uses a larger step. In the slide navigator, use the labeled Move Up and Move Down commands when drag-and-drop is inconvenient.

Figure Tool keeps visible focus indicators and labels for main controls. Color alone should not carry scientific meaning: add text, line styles, markers, or patterns and review contrast at the final export size.

Canvas zoom changes the view, not document geometry. Use Fit Figure or Fit Slide to restore an overview; presentation playback fits the complete slide while keeping navigation and Exit controls reachable.

sections.title: Troubleshooting missing or unsupported content
sections.summary: Resolve missing artwork and compatibility warnings without hiding or overwriting the source problem.
body: If a scientific asset is missing, confirm that the installed Asset Library is available, search by the asset name shown in Source & notes, and reinsert only after saving a copy. Released assets should not require a repository or network path.
If a font is unavailable, keep PDF text as outlines for visual fidelity or choose an installed replacement and review wrapping. Figure check reports text that is overset or likely to need attention.
If PDF or SVG content opens as protected artwork, use an editable overlay or release only the supported portion. Keep the original source attached until the result has passed a visual comparison.

If PPTX import reports unsupported content, keep the original PPTX, review every warning, and decide whether to retain a flattened visual, redraw the object, or omit it deliberately. SmartArt, charts, tables, media, animation, macros, OLE, freeform paths, and advanced masters are not silently converted.

If a save, import, or export fails, do not close the document. Save As to a new location when possible, note the operation and file type, then open Help > Troubleshooting details for the technical message.

sections.title: About Figure Tool
sections.summary: Figure Tool 1.0.0-beta.6 is the scientific Figure and Presentation editor within Mersich Lab Superbench.
body: Figure Tool combines a single-canvas Figure workspace and a multi-slide Presentation workspace with shared vector, text, shape, connector, scientific-asset, style, save, and export foundations.
Mersich Lab Superbench is in active v1 development. The editor version shown here is not a claim of a public v1 release.
Open Figure and Present in Mersich Lab Superbench. Direct editor launch surfaces remain available for development and qualification.

sections.title: Known limitations and protected imported content
sections.summary: Some PDF, SVG, PPTX, typography, presentation, and collaboration behavior remains deliberately bounded in this beta.
body: Figure Tool keeps the original PDF attached to the document and retains parsed structure when available, but its current canvas edit model reconstructs supported artwork through vector conversion. PDF text opens as outlines for fidelity and can be explicitly converted to editable runs with a reversible Keep outlines action.

Editable PDF text can require font substitution, symbol normalization, spacing review, or rotated-label adjustment. Clip, mask, filter, blend, gradient, mesh, and pattern structures are editable only when Figure Tool can represent the specific case safely; otherwise the original appearance remains protected.

Figure Tool does not claim arbitrary PDF rewriting, complete prepress or color-management support, native Illustrator equivalence, or faithful reconstruction of every SVG or PDF effect. Review important imported and exported artwork visually.

PPTX v1 is limited to the common objects listed in PowerPoint and Google Slides compatibility. Character-range superscript, subscript, baseline shift, and mixed formatting are reduced to the text object's base style with a warning. Theme, master, layout, chart, SmartArt, table, media, animation, macro, OLE, 3D, arbitrary freeform-path, and advanced-effect fidelity is not provided. Universal PowerPoint or Google Slides round-tripping is not claimed.
Presentation mode does not provide animation authoring, real-time collaboration, comments/review parity, or direct Google Slides cloud integration. File interchange uses PPTX, PDF, SVG, and PNG.
Raster vectorization reconstructs pixel regions for editing; it does not infer biological meaning, statistics, labels, or experimental context. Figure Tool does not validate scientific conclusions.
Recovery copies and unsaved-work prompts reduce accidental loss but are not version control or cloud backup. Keep deliberate saved versions of important Figure and Presentation documents.
